items.definition:
a blemish or flaw
The scratch was a mar on the otherwise perfect surface.

a record of events year by year
The annal recorded the major events of the kingdom.

Intense happiness; the ability to find appropriate expression for one's thoughts.
She expressed her thoughts with great felicity.

The study and treatment of tumors
She decided to specialize in oncology.

a particle representing a quantum of light or other electromagnetic radiation
Light is composed of tiny particles called photons.

a Turkish title of respect or honor
The bey ruled over the province for many years.

A compound consisting of two or more amino acids linked in a chain.
Peptides play a crucial role in biological processes.

a chronic disease involving hardening of body tissue
Multiple sclerosis affects the brain and spinal cord.

a measure of the disorder or randomness of a system
The universe tends towards increasing entropy.

cancer of the lymphatic system
He was diagnosed with lymphoma last year.

the devising or choosing of names for things, especially in a science or other discipline
The scientific nomenclature for plants can be complex.

Messenger ribonucleic acid, a type of RNA that carries genetic information from DNA to the ribosome.
mRNA vaccines use messenger RNA to teach our cells how to make a protein.

a branch of mathematics
Topology is a complex field of mathematics.

the thickening and scarring of connective tissue
Pulmonary fibrosis affects the lungs.

a circular opening, especially at the apex of a dome
The Pantheon in Rome is famous for its large oculus.

resistance to an alternating current
The engineer measured the electrical impedance of the circuit.

each of two or more forms of the same element
Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope used in dating ancient artifacts.

The theory or philosophy of law
She specialized in comparative jurisprudence during her law studies.

leadership or dominance, especially by one state or social group over others
The country sought to establish its hegemony over the region.

A unit of phonological weight or a genus of trees
In phonology, a long vowel can be considered to have two moras.

an expression of more than two algebraic terms
We learned how to factor a quadratic polynomial in math class.

sexual attraction to children
Pedophilia is a serious crime.

An organelle found in large numbers in most cells, in which the biochemical processes of respiration and energy production occur.
The mitochondrion is often called the powerhouse of the cell.

a localized, blood-filled balloon-like bulge in the wall of a blood vessel
He suffered a brain aneurysm.

the district or see of an archbishop
The archdiocese covers several counties.

a substance formed in or necessary for metabolism
Researchers are studying the various metabolites produced by the bacteria.

the protection, backing, or support of a particular person or organization
The project was launched under the aegis of the United Nations.

a positively charged ion (NH4+)
Ammonium compounds are often used in fertilizers.

A descendant of a notable family.
He was a scion of a wealthy banking family.

a mathematical object
In physics, a tensor is a geometric object that describes linear relations between geometric vectors, scalars, and other tensors.

imaging by sections
CT scans use X-ray tomography to create detailed images of the body.

a ghost or ghostlike image of someone
He saw a pale wraith disappear into the mist.

belief in the abolition of all government
Anarchism advocates for a society without rulers.

a statement or proposition which is regarded as being established, accepted, or self-evidently true
It is an axiom that a straight line is the shortest distance between two points.

a group of eye conditions
Glaucoma can lead to blindness if not treated.

Regular payment made into a fund by an employee toward a future pension
Employees contribute to their superannuation fund each month.

a compound consisting of a nucleoside linked to a phosphate group
DNA is made up of long chains of nucleotides.

the branch of molecular biology concerned with the structure, function, evolution, and mapping of genomes
Advances in genomics are revolutionizing personalized medicine.

a lout or hooligan, especially one who drives recklessly (Australian/NZ slang)
The police issued a warning to the hoons doing burnouts in the car park.

common sense; practical intelligence
He showed considerable nous in handling the difficult situation.

a tract of grassland; a ley line
Ancient monuments are often said to be built along ley lines.

a turn or change, especially in poetry or music
The volta in the sonnet marked a shift in tone.

the process of gradually writing off the initial cost of an asset
The loan's amortization schedule showed the principal and interest payments over time.

a powerful, highly addictive stimulant drug
The police seized a large quantity of methamphetamine.

lack of power or ability to act
The government's impotence in the face of the crisis was evident.

the fact of two things being seen or placed close together with contrasting effect
The artist used juxtaposition to highlight the differences.

An enzyme that synthesizes long chains of polymers.
DNA polymerase plays a crucial role in DNA replication.

the measurement of spectra
Mass spectrometry is used to identify unknown compounds.

a laboratory technique for the separation of a mixture
Chromatography is used to separate pigments in plants.

a condition characterized by an excess of watery fluid accumulating in the body
The doctor diagnosed the patient with edema in their legs.

Disinterested and selfless concern for the well-being of others.
His act of altruism saved many lives.

the abandonment or renunciation of a religious or political belief
His public declaration of atheism was seen by some as an act of apostasy.

the death of most or all of the cells in an organ or tissue due to disease, injury, or failure of the blood supply
The doctor explained that the tissue damage was due to necrosis.

A chemical element
Selenium is an essential trace element for humans.

A compound of sulfur with another element or group
Hydrogen sulfide is a toxic gas.

A taxonomic group of any rank, such as a species, family, or class
Humans belong to the taxon Homo sapiens.

one of two or more alternative forms of a gene
Each parent contributes one allele for every gene.

a compound containing the hydroxide ion
Sodium hydroxide is a strong base used in many industrial processes.

a magician or sorcerer
The ancient text described a powerful magus who could control the elements.

the addition of a methyl group to a substrate
DNA methylation plays a crucial role in gene expression.

a chief magistrate of a town or district
The reeve was responsible for maintaining order in the village.

the process by which molecules adhere to a surface
The experiment studied the adsorption of gases on metal surfaces.

the theory of knowledge, especially with regard to its methods, validity, and scope
His research focuses on the epistemology of science.

a glottal stop in Arabic
The hamza is an important phoneme in Arabic pronunciation.
